title: Question Bank Tagging and Generation
summary: Turn years of DPPs, module books and past papers into a clean, syllabus-tagged question bank, remove duplicates and draft new variants that faculty check before any student sees them.

seo.title: Question Bank Tagging and Generation with AI | VipraTech
seo.description: AI that extracts questions from Word, PDF and scans, tags them by syllabus, type and difficulty, removes duplicates and drafts variants for faculty review.

problem.intro: Most coaching institutes and edtech companies own a large question collection that is hard to use: daily practice problems in Word files, module books as PDFs, scanned previous-year papers and solutions typed by different faculty over many years. Building a balanced test means searching folders from memory, and the same question reappears under different numbering.

pain_points.title: Untagged content
pain_points.detail: Questions lack consistent chapter, topic, difficulty and question-type tags, so test setters cannot filter by syllabus or balance a paper.

pain_points.title: Equations and diagrams break on import
pain_points.detail: MathType objects, scanned figures and chemical structures do not survive copying into the test platform.

pain_points.title: Hidden duplicates
pain_points.detail: The same question sits in several modules with small edits, so students see repeats and analytics double count.

pain_points.title: New questions take faculty time
pain_points.detail: Writing fresh numericals and variants for every test series competes with teaching hours.

solution.overview: We build a content pipeline that ingests Word files, PDFs and scans, splits them into question, options, answer key and solution, and converts equations to LaTeX or MathML with figures kept as images. Each question is tagged against your syllabus tree, for example the published JEE Main or NEET-UG syllabus, with question type, a difficulty estimate and source. Near-duplicates are clustered for a faculty member to merge. For generation, faculty pick a question and ask for variants; the system changes values or context, re-derives the answer with a solver where possible and queues every draft for review. Nothing reaches students without faculty approval.
capabilities: Splits mixed documents into question, options, answer key and worked solution
Converts equations to LaTeX or MathML and keeps diagrams as linked images
Tags syllabus chapter, topic, question type, difficulty estimate and source
Clusters near-duplicate questions across modules and years for faculty to merge
Drafts numerical and conceptual variants, with answers re-derived by a solver where possible
Exports to your test platform in its import format, such as Excel, QTI or API

workflow.title: Ingest content
workflow.detail: Word files, PDFs, scanned papers and existing platform exports are loaded subject by subject.

workflow.title: Split and convert
workflow.detail: Each item is separated into its parts, and equations and figures are converted into a format the test platform can render.

workflow.title: Tag and de-duplicate
workflow.detail: Questions are tagged against your syllabus tree and near-duplicates are clustered.

workflow.title: Verify answers and tags
workflow.detail: Low-confidence tags, missing keys and answers the solver disagrees with are queued for faculty.

workflow.title: Faculty review
workflow.detail: Subject faculty correct tags, merge duplicates and approve or reject generated variants.

workflow.title: Publish to the bank
workflow.detail: Approved questions are pushed to the test platform with full metadata and source history.

inputs: DPPs, assignments and module books in Word or PDF
Your syllabus tree and tagging conventions
Existing question exports from the test platform
Seed questions chosen by faculty for variant generation
outputs: Structured question bank with LaTeX or MathML and figures
Syllabus, type, difficulty and source tags
Import files or API pushes for your test platform
human_in_the_loop: Subject faculty approve tag corrections, duplicate merges and every generated question before it enters the live bank. Difficulty tags start as estimates and are updated from real student attempt data once tests run.
integrations: Shared drives holding faculty Word files
guardrails: Generated questions remain drafts until a named faculty member approves them
Answers rechecked with a solver; disagreements go to faculty
Source recorded for every question so third-party copyrighted material can be identified and excluded
No student data used for generation
Version history kept so any change can be traced and reversed
compliance_notes: Questions drawn from published books or other institutes' material may be protected by copyright; the source tag helps your team decide what can be reused.

pilot.scope: One subject for one exam, for example JEE Main physics, using one module series and its matching previous-year papers.
deliverables: Syllabus tree and tagging rules agreed with faculty
Structured, tagged bank for the pilot subject
Set of generated variants with faculty review outcomes
Import into your test platform and a roll-out plan

what_we_measure.how: Faculty review of a random sample of tagged questions per chapter.
Clusters confirmed by faculty as true duplicates or near-duplicates.
Generated variants approved, edited or rejected by faculty, with reasons.
Questions that display incorrectly in the test platform after import.

faqs.a: Not always, which is why none are published without faculty review. Numerical answers are re-derived with a solver where possible, and any disagreement is flagged. The pilot reports how many drafts faculty accepted, edited or rejected.

faqs.q: Can it handle chemistry structures and physics diagrams?
faqs.a: Diagrams and structures are extracted as images linked to the question, and equations become LaTeX or MathML. Complex figures can be redrawn later, but nothing is lost in conversion.

faqs.q: Do we keep ownership of our content?
faqs.a: Yes. The bank, tags and generated questions belong to you and are stored in your environment. We use models that do not train on your data.

faqs.q: Can we use our own syllabus structure?
faqs.a: Yes. We map to your chapter and topic tree, whether that follows the JEE or NEET syllabus, a state board or your own module order.
